profile.name: Kale Bittner
profile.motivations:
In 2016, I learned what money truly is—not just a government-issued piece of paper, but faith in a system. To have faith in any system, I need to believe in the rules that underpin it. This belief led me to Bitcoin and, soon after, to Cardano. Since 2017, I’ve been a dedicated member of the ecosystem. While I’m not an influencer or programmer, I’ve remained actively engaged—first as a holder, then as an ITN delegator, as a DeFi participant, and now as a DRep.

I’m not one to push any cryptocurrency, but I’m always eager to share the vision when asked. I believe in Cardano, I believe in its community, and I bring a perspective shaped by years of quiet, meaningful involvement. Having witnessed the challenges and triumphs over the past 7-8 years, I’m now ready to be a voice that helps guide us forward.
profile.objectives:
As a DRep, I am committed to upholding principles of fair and sensible governance, ensuring that power is balanced and distributed in a way that reflects the needs and interests of the broader community. I believe that governance should empower citizens, foster healthy debate, and encourage constructive criticism as essential components of growth and innovation.

I will strive to maintain these ideals as we navigate the complexities of governance, ensuring that decisions are made with a long-term perspective and a focus on the collective good. I recognize that for Cardano to be more than just a best-in-class cryptocurrency, it must become a model for governance—one that demonstrates how decentralized, inclusive decision-making can lead to sustainable success.

By prioritizing transparency, inclusivity, and collaboration, I will do my part to ensure that Cardano not only excels in technology but also leads by example in building a governance framework that can be a blueprint for the fut
profile.qualifications:
I’ll be transparent: I’m not a programmer, and I’ll defer to the expertise of others when it comes to the technical details of programming adjustments. However, I am an executive at a media / tech company, and I specialize in gathering input from diverse stakeholders to make decisions that align with long-term goals. My focus is on marketing, adoption, and game theory, and I will bring my expertise to the functional aspects of Cardano’s governance.

I’ve often told my friends that while it’s important to understand the rules, it’s far better to write them. Over my career, I’ve spent years analyzing rules, contracts, and systems to identify pitfalls, avoid manipulation, and ensure fairness. Good governance is like a good game—the best ones are built on rules that everyone can agree on, and that’s the kind of governance I strive for.

profile.name: RobertAriano
profile.motivations: Why I want to be a DRep has to do with the opportunity to be held more liable to vote on proposals within the Ecosystem. Becoming a DRep would allow me to speak on behalf of others who are not as involved in day to day with Cardano. Personal experiences I would like to share is how Cardano has helped bring my work to life in every aspect, on a personal level as well as professionally. As a professional business owner I can be trusted as a DRep due to responsibilities I have encountered. Also, I am involved heavily with Project Catalyst and have been a community reviewer for three funds. This shows I am willing to get involved and make a difference for the Cardano community.
profile.objectives: As a DRep, I believe that embracing the privileges set forth in relation to the Cardano Constitution will help Cardano become an underlying technology in every sector of business and personal life. What I would like to achieve as a DRep is the opportunity to use our product to get more people involved in the Cardano Ecosystem. Due to the Cardano Development Portal being a major part of the Cardano Ecosystem, I believe this tool can be viewed every day by millions of users. My goal is to make the Cardano Portal visible in relation to tasks performed through its use. Not only does it get folks interested in development on our ecosystem, but it also shows them how to get involved in governance within Cardano
profile.qualifications: I am a Cardano Blockchain Certified Associate and am very much interested in peer-reviewed research within Cardano and IOHK. I spent years performing research at the PhD level and am happy to assist others who would like to learn more about Peer-review. These qualifications are relevant for my role as a DRep because it shows I have the ability to finish what I have started. Voting on others behalf's is important to the individual, as well as the community.

profile.name: Marian[ALOOP]SPO
profile.motivations:
I think everyone should be their own DRep. It avoids centralization of the voting power and allows you to voice your opinion
I never planned on being a DRep but after some consideration I decided to become one. Main reason: to represent myself but others are welcome.
profile.objectives: I will continue supporting the infrastructure as an SPO, and I will try to focus as a DRep in what's best for Cardano; decentralization, security, innovation and mostly prevent milking funds from treasury (aka Guardian of the Galaxy)
profile.qualifications:
Single pool operator. I have been a stakepool operator of the pool ALOOP since 6/2021 on Mainnet and 1/2021 on Testnet. 
I have worked as a System Engineer for the last 15 years with extensive IT background since early '90s 
I stay informed about the development in Cardano, member of xSPO, CSPA and a passive member on Intersect Discord (mostly reading and taking notes)
